conflicts.fact: Which lesson quantifies atmospheric pressure and explains why our bodies are not crushed
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 says Lesson 4 will quantify exactly how large atmospheric pressure is and why our bodies are not crushed. Lesson 4 quantifies atmospheric pressure (~101.3 kPa), but its explained summary never addresses why bodies are not crushed and only raises it as a DQB question. Lesson 1 had already given the body explanation.

conflicts.fact: What the jerrycan phenomenon is: sealed empty jerrycan crushed by air removal vs the anchoring description of a jerrycan; also Lesson 1 vs the unit's description of when the model began
conflicts.versions: Lesson 8 says the cumulative model was updated 'since Lesson 1' as a liquid-container cross-section and says 'growing with us since Lesson 4'; Lessons 1-7 describe the model as a jerrycan with force arrows. Lesson 8 contradicts itself and the others on what the model is and when it began.

conflicts.fact: Whether liquid pressure depends on container shape/area and what 'independent' means; also derivation framing of P=ρgh as new
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 introduces P = ρgh with worked calculations at Naivasha towers and states it as already taught. Lesson 8 presents the derivation and calculation of P = ρgh as new ('building on Lessons 3 and 6'), duplicating the same content, and Lesson 3's DQB expects P = ρgh to be the next step, so the sequence is out of order.

conflicts.fact: Mass/load used in syringe investigation and who introduces Pascal's Principle
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 uses a 50 g mass on the small plunger and measures the large plunger rise, and derives Pascal's Principle. Lesson 7 says it 'rebuilds the Lesson 5 model with a heavier 200 g load' and places the mass on the large plunger, contradicting the setup in Lesson 5. Also the syringe tube length is 30 cm vs about 40 cm.

conflicts.fact: Whether Lesson 1's jerrycan recovered shape and the 'full' jerrycan explanation vs Lesson 9 re-inflation; also number of lessons in the unit
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says the unit spans the next 19 lessons (20 total) and that the jerrycan partially recovered on reopening. Lesson 9 is the unit synthesis lesson closing the DQB ('nine lessons'), and says the jerrycan re-inflated to its original shape with a pump.

conflicts.fact: Lesson 9 says the Lesson 1 prediction cards were kept by the teacher, while Lesson 1 says students keep their models and write predictions in exercise books
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1: predictions written in exercise books and recorded on the chalkboard; models stay with students. Lesson 9: teacher returns original Lesson 1 prediction cards 'kept from Lesson 1'. Lesson 4 also says DQB index cards were posted in Lesson 1 with predictions, while Lesson 1 used sticky notes.

conflicts.fact: Atmospheric pressure value and Nairobi pressure
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 gives ~101.3 kPa, Lesson 8 gives ~100,000 Pa (equal to 10 m of fresh water), Lesson 9 gives 101,325 Pa and Nairobi ~83,000 Pa; Lesson 8's 'equivalent to 10 m of fresh water' conflicts with its own calculation of ~102,500 Pa at 10 m in seawater being approximately atmospheric.

conflicts.fact: How the demonstration removes air and which phenomenon is replayed
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 uses a bicycle hand pump fitted with a one-way valve or hot water then sealing. Lesson 4 describes the tin as a replay and says steam pushes air out. Lesson 9 says the jerrycan collapse was observed with Boyle's Law, which is never taught in Lessons 1-8.
